entities.summary: Harbinder Singh is a former field hockey player from India. He started his international career in 1961 at the age of 18 years [youngest member of the team] with a tour to New Zealand and Australia with Indian hockey team. During the span of 12 years from 1961 to 1972 had represented the country in three Olympics – Tokyo 1964 — gold medal, Mexico 1968 — bronze medal and was also selected as a centre forward in the "World XI", in Munich 1972 — bronze medal. Harbinder Singh was a athletes & competitors from Quetta (b. 1943-07-08, Quetta). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key member of India's hockey team, Harbinder Singh contributed to the country's first-ever Olympic gold medal in Tokyo 1964, while also representing the nation at three Olympics and earning recognition as a centre forward in the 'World XI'. His achievements had a significant impact on Indian sports history.
